{{Short description|American biologist (born 1961)}}

'''Grant R. Woods''' (born 1961)<ref name="Outdoor Life 3"/> is an American biologist specializing in [[white tail deer]] and associated land management that increases deer populations, primarily for hunting purposes.<ref name="Outdoor Life">{{cite web|url=https://www.outdoorlife.com/articles/hunting/2014/10/mind-rutting-buck/|title=Whitetail Deer: Into the Mind of a Rutting Buck|author=Tony Hansen|journal=Outdoor Life|date=November 17, 2014}}</ref><ref name="Field and Stream">{{cite web|url=https://www.fieldandstream.com/bring-more-deer-to-your-tree-stand-with-poor-mans-food-plot/|title=Bring More Deer to Your Tree Stand With a Poor-Man's Food Plot|author=Scott Bestul|journal=Field and Stream|date=August 1, 2004}}</ref>

==Personal==
Woods is married and has two daughters.  He lives near [[Branson, MO]].<ref name="Bass Pro">{{cite web|url=https://1source.basspro.com/user/dr-grant-woods|title=Dr. Grant Woods bio|publisher=Bass Pro Shops}}</ref>

==Education==
Woods has a Ph.D. in Forest Resources from [[Clemson University]], a master's degree in biology from [[Southwest Missouri State University]], and a B.S. in Zoology/Computer Information Systems, also from Southwest Missouri State University.<ref name="Woods CV">{{cite web|url=https://www.growingdeer.tv/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/Professional-experience-for-Dr.-Grant-Woods.pdf|title=Grant R. Woods CV}}</ref><ref name="Bass Pro"/>

==Career==
Woods is well known as a consultant on land management for increasing deer herds.  He is the founder of growingdeer.com, and is noted for his ability to explain complex technical items in everyday language for hunters managing their lands.  His research areas include the pioneering use of remote-activated cameras to record bucks using [[deer rub]]s during [[Rut (mammalian reproduction)|rutting season]].<ref name="Outdoor Life 2">{{cite web|url=https://www.outdoorlife.com/19-huntings-fishing-shooting-conservation-influencers/|title=The Influencers: 19 People Who Have Changed the Outdoors (for Better and for Worse)|journal=Outdoor Life|date=November 20, 2017}}</ref>

In 2001, Woods and his wife bought property in the [[Ozark]]s of [[Missouri]] and over 20 years transformed it into a lush habitat for wildlife.  The 1500 acre property was known as the "Proving Grounds".  Prior to Woods buying it, it was an abandoned cattle ranch. The improvement process comprised first eradicating invasive species, such as [[lespedeza]], [[multiflora rose]], and [[knapweed]], using selective application of herbicides.  Woods then used [[controlled burn]]s to stimulate the germination of native seeds in the soil.  By Woods' estimate, some of the germinated seeds were over 75 years old.  He then added "food plots" to provide forage and cover.<ref name="Outdoor Life 3">{{cite web|url=https://www.outdoorlife.com/conservation/grant-woods-sold-proving-grounds/|title=Grant Woods Just Sold the "Proving Grounds." Here’s What He Learned from Building One of the Most Famous Whitetail Properties in America|author=Katie Hill|journal=Outdoor Life|date=September 16, 2022}}</ref>

In 2021, Woods sold the property and began developing another 900 acre plot known as "Proving Grounds 2.0". Since he was 61 as of 2022, his goal is to develop the land in 1/4 of the time (i.e., 5 years).  He also largely eliminated the use of pesticides and herbicides and used a "no erosion" form of roads called "broad-based dips" developed at Clemson.<ref name="Outdoor Life 3"/>

==Awards and honors==
